subject.title: Discord routing: mention > reply-target > default owner (suppress default owner when targeted)

question: Should explicit Discord bot mentions and replied-to bot identity override existing channel bindings/default ownership, with every non-target account suppressed, and should bot-authored replies use the same precedence?
rationale: The source gap is concrete, but changing metadata from a mention gate into routing authority alters existing multi-account binding semantics and bot-to-bot activation behavior.

options.title: Adopt Discord target precedence
options.body: Make explicit bot mentions and replied-to bot identity authoritative before channel-owner fallback, with non-target handlers suppressed.

options.title: Keep bindings authoritative
options.body: Continue using mentions and replies only for activation while requiring explicit bindings or focus commands to select another agent.

options.title: Add an opt-in policy
options.body: Preserve current defaults and introduce a Discord configuration switch for targeted-bot routing, at the cost of another compatibility-sensitive config surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt Discord target precedence
recommendation.body: Make explicit bot mentions and replied-to bot identity authoritative before channel-owner fallback, with non-target handlers suppressed.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the latest issue-level product analysis and are connected by history to the central Discord preflight and routing surfaces.
